question.text: Saraswati Growth Fund is a SEBI-registered Category II AIF set up as a contributory, determinate, irrevocable trust. In the financial year starting April 1, 2025, the fund earns INR 80 crore of dividend and interest and INR 25 crore categorised (post Finance Act 2025) as capital gains on transfer of unlisted equity. From the MANAGER's perspective, which statement best describes the fund-level tax treatment of these two income streams under Section 115UB read with Section 10(23FBA) of the ITA?

answer.text: Both income streams are taxed at the fund level at MMR because AIFs do not enjoy pass-through.
Both income streams are exempt in the fund's hands and chargeable directly to the unit-holders in the same character in which they arose.
Dividend/interest is exempt at the fund; capital gains are taxed at the fund at 12.5%.
Only dividends enjoy pass-through; interest and capital gains are taxed at the fund at MMR.

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 115UB read with Section 10(23FBA) gives Cat I and Cat II AIFs tax pass-through status for all income other than business income. Dividend, interest and capital gains flow through to unit-holders in the same character in which the fund earned them (workbook pages 447-448). With effect from the financial year starting April 1, 2025, the Finance Act 2025 amendment to Section 2(14) expressly treats securities held by Cat I/II AIFs as capital assets, so the INR 25 crore is capital gains that passes through. The Trap: Option A confuses Cat III (fund-level tax) with Cat I/II. Option C invents a fund-level capital-gains charge that does not exist for pass-through funds. Option D wrongly splits the streams - pass-through is uniform across all non-business income heads. Note: The Finance Act 2025 capital-asset classification applies from the financial year beginning April 1, 2025; the stem timing aligns with that effective date.
